findings.title: Test reads the port and makes the login call in one return statement, but Go does not fix their order.
findings.body:
`return gotPort, runner.authLogin(...)` puts two things in one return statement. One is a plain read of `gotPort`. The other is the call that sets it, because `OpenBrowser` runs inside `authLogin`. The Go spec guarantees left-to-right order only among function calls. It does not say whether a plain variable is read before or after a call in the same statement.

Today's compiler happens to run the call first, so the test passes. A compiler that reads `gotPort` first would return 0, and the success cases would fail with `callback port = 0`.

Fix: run the login on its own line first, then return the port.
findings.suggestion:
err = runner.authLogin(context.Background(), env, c.args)
				return gotPort, err
